title: Córdobas
desc: Money that is not yours yet

sn.e: I need to buy water.

sn.s: Aquí uno compra el agua en bolsa o en botella.
sn.e: Here you buy water in a bag or a bottle.

sn.s: Voy a comprar agua y algo de comer.
sn.e: I am going to buy water and something to eat.

sn.s: Hace calor y no tengo agua en el cuarto.
sn.e: It is hot and I have no water in my room.

sn.s: Doña Carmen me dice dónde comprar.
sn.e: Doña Carmen tells me where to buy it.
"On the corner," she says.

sn.s: Voy a la esquina de la calle.
sn.e: I go to the corner of the street.

sn.s: Hay una señora con una mesa.
sn.e: There is a woman with a table.

sn.s: En la mesa hay agua, pan y fruta.
sn.e: On the table there is water, bread and fruit.
"Buenas," I say.
"Buenas," the woman says.
"How much does the water cost?" I ask.
"Fifteen," the woman says.
"Fifteen what?" I ask.
The woman laughs.
"Fifteen pesos, young man."
I do not understand.

sn.s: Aquí la plata se llama córdoba.
sn.e: Here the money is called the córdoba.
But people say pesos.

sn.s: Córdoba en el papel, peso en la boca.
sn.e: Córdoba on the paper, peso in the mouth.

sn.s: Le doy un billete de cien córdobas.
sn.e: I give her a hundred-córdoba note.

sn.s: La señora me da el vuelto.
sn.e: The woman gives me my change.
I count the change slowly.
Eighty-five córdobas.
That is right.
"Thank you," I say.
Then I buy bread.
"How much does the bread cost?" I ask.
"Ten pesos," the woman says.
Buying bread costs little.

sn.s: Comprar agua cuesta un poco más.
sn.e: Buying water costs a little more.

sn.s: Todo lo que compro hoy es barato.
sn.e: Everything I buy today is cheap.

sn.s: Yo pago con un billete grande.
sn.e: I pay with a big note.

sn.s: La señora dice que no es caro.
sn.e: The woman says it is not expensive.
Here things cost little.

sn.s: Un vaso de agua no cuesta nada.
sn.e: A glass of water costs nothing.

sn.s: Pero un taxi puede costar mucho.
sn.e: But a taxi can cost a lot.

sn.s: Pero uno tiene que preguntar cuánto cuesta.
sn.e: But you have to ask how much it costs.
And then you pay.

sn.s: Nunca se paga antes de preguntar.
sn.e: You never pay before asking.

sn.s: Eso es barato y eso es caro.
sn.e: That is cheap and that is expensive.
Ten córdobas for the bread.
That is cheap.

sn.s: Todo aquí es barato para mí.
sn.e: Everything here is cheap for me.

sn.s: Pero no es barato para la gente de aquí.
sn.e: But it is not cheap for the people here.
I understand that later.

sn.s: Aquí hay que saber lo que cuesta cada cosa.
sn.e: Here you have to know what each thing costs.

sn.s: En la casa le enseño el pan a Roberto.
sn.e: At the house I show Roberto the bread.
"How much did you pay?" Roberto asks.
"Ten pesos," I say.
"That is right," Roberto says.
"And the water?" he asks.
"Fifteen pesos."
"That is right too."

sn.s: Entonces Roberto me pregunta por el taxi.
sn.e: Then Roberto asks me about the taxi.
"How much did you pay from the airport?"

sn.s: No me acuerdo bien del número.
sn.e: I do not remember the number properly.

sn.s: Le enseño lo que tengo en la mano.
sn.e: I show him what I have in my hand.
Roberto's eyes open wide.
"Ideay! That is very expensive."
"Expensive?" I ask.
"Very expensive. You paid four times over."

sn.s: Doña Carmen se ríe desde la cocina.
sn.e: Doña Carmen laughs from the kitchen.

sn.s: "Al chele siempre le cobran caro", dice.
sn.e: "They always charge the chele more," she says.
Roberto teaches me one thing.
"First ask how much it costs."
"Always. Before you get in the taxi."

sn.s: "Y si es muy caro, uno no paga."
sn.e: "And if it is too expensive, you do not pay."
"And what do I say?" I ask.
"Say: that's too expensive."
"That's too expensive," I say.
"Like that," Roberto says. "Again."
"That's too expensive."
"Now you've got it," Roberto says.
That night I count my money.

sn.s: Tengo menos plata de la que pensaba.
sn.e: I have less money than I thought.
The taxi cost me a lot.

sn.s: El agua me costó quince pesos.
sn.e: The water cost me fifteen pesos.

sn.s: El pan me costó diez pesos.
sn.e: The bread cost me ten pesos.

sn.s: Y ahora sé cuánto cuestan las cosas.
sn.e: And now I know how much things cost.
Tomorrow I am going to ask first.
